title: Ecosystem attribute markers and implementer-aware compatibility policy
question: How is the supported surface marked and which changes count as compatible?

options.text: Attributes + explicit named-argument stance (chosen): Machine-readable, ecosystem-aligned.
Keep docblock tags and location publication: 97 unmarked types and no member/kind data.

context: Independent architecture review (revision 2) requested by the owner (brief M6, M7). Phase tasks and implementation remain deferred. Refines D4 without contradicting it.
decision: Mark the surface with AzGuard-owned #[Api(since)] and #[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Implement|Call, since)] attributes, exclude members with @internal, and end location-based publication. Cover parameter names of Api methods, constructors and factories (opt-out @no-named-arguments); core calls Implement SPI methods positionally. Classify each public enum as closed or open. Adding interface/abstract methods, parameters to overridable methods, changing defaults or adding cases to closed enums are breaks after 1.0. The generator records attributes, members, overrides, constants, enum cases and facade methods derived from AzGuard\AzGuard.
rationale: CoreX, Chatom and Commerz use the same attribute scheme. PHP binds named arguments to the runtime implementation, so implementer renames are only safe if core calls positionally; the AzGuard DSL is named-argument oriented, so its consumer parameter names must be stable. Symfony's BC promise shows the same consumer/implementer split.
consequences: About 250 types gain attributes in P2.
A static rule checks positional SPI calls (I20).

evidence.note: Owner requested an independent review and authorized amending Codex decisions within the owner principles.
